cards.explanation: The answer is that Moses already gave them land east of the Jordan. The text says, "For Moses had given the inheritance east of the Jordan to the other two and a half tribes." (Joshua 14:3). Their slice was already off the tray before the lot-drawing started. Nobody was left out of the line, friends, they had just been served early.

The answer is cities. The text says no portion of the land went to the Levites, "…except for cities in which to live, along with pasturelands for their flocks and herds." (Joshua 14:4). So the Levites had places to live and room for their animals. Not a bad deal, friends.

The answer is that Caleb remained loyal to the LORD. He says, "…I remained loyal to the LORD my God." (Joshua 14:8). Right before that, he says his brothers who went with him made the hearts of the people melt with fear. Those two things sit side by side, and Caleb puts himself on the loyal side. That's a line worth hanging onto, bakers.

The answer is the land his feet had walked on. Moses swore, "…the land on which you have set foot will be an inheritance to you and your children forever, because you have wholly followed the LORD my God." (Joshua 14:9). Notice the reason Moses gives, friends. Caleb had wholly followed the LORD, and the promise was attached to the ground under his feet.
The answer is eighty-five, and Caleb says so himself: "…here I am today, eighty-five years old…" (Joshua 14:10). Forty plus forty-five does it. Math works even when the oven's on, bakers.

The answer is True. Caleb says he's "…still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out." Then he adds, "As my strength was then, so it is now for war, for going out, and for coming in." (Joshua 14:11). Eighty-five and ready to go, friends. I'm over here stretching just to reach the top shelf.

The answer is with the LORD's help. Caleb says, "Perhaps with the LORD’s help I will drive them out, as the LORD has spoken." (Joshua 14:12). Just before, he says he's still strong for war (Joshua 14:11). He also names the Anakim's great and fortified cities. And when he talks about driving them out, he names the LORD's help, friends.

The answer is False. Joshua doesn't send Caleb away. The text says, "Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance." (Joshua 14:13). Caleb got the blessing and the land, friends.

The answer is Anakim. The text says Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba, "…after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim." (Joshua 14:15). Those are the same Anakim mentioned earlier, with their great and fortified cities (Joshua 14:12). Fancy name, bakers, but Hebron suits it better.
